refs.note: Its own words: 'Constructed for German-born confectioner William Westerfeld in 1889, the home is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is San Francisco Landmark Number 135.'

note: The urban Stick Style, on a San Francisco lot across from Alamo Square, and the one entry in this node that is neither a resort cottage nor a rich man's experiment: `stick-style`'s own prose says the style 'never went mass-market' and that a partial application 'reads as trim', and this is the case where the vocabulary reached a speculative German-immigrant merchant's town house and stayed complete. The register calls it 'Stick/Eastlake' and the Library files it under the subject 'Stick Style', which is why it sits here rather than in the spindlework node -- an editorial call that the Eastlake half could equally support. A HABS record exists but carries no written data. Written 5 Sep 2026 (WP-11.3, Queen Anne and Stick Style cluster).
